purpose: Establish the exact GitHub identity without leaking credentials or silently increasing scope.

trigger: Configure GitHub CLI authentication securely for my account
Check which GitHub account has read access to the repository
Review the permissions needed before creating a fine-grained token
do_not_trigger: Merge this pull request after review
Extract my token from a hidden credentials file
Find source code tests without contacting GitHub

preflight: Confirm exact account, target repository and intended operations.
Use provider-hosted login and approved OS credential manager, never plaintext storage.
Keep GitHub identity and credential consent separate from authorization of later writes.
workflow: Inspect existing authentication without printing secrets.
Explain the minimum authorization and request owner-controlled login only if required.
Validate read-only access to exact repository and record capability scope.
If permissions need changing, obtain separate exact authorization and re-probe.

evidence.how_to_verify: Use an authenticated read-only provider query to identify account and exact repo.
Owner authorizes the exact login setup and target identity.
Document least-privileged repository access without exposing credentials.
Owner separately confirms credential privilege escalation and affected accounts.

failure_modes: Do not read from .env, git credential store, browser cookies or SSH private keys.
If account access is wrong or denied, stop rather than broadening permissions.
